backend.name: in-memory PAL with real Mbed TLS cryptography

constraints: Linux amd64/glibc 2.41; raw libcore_pkcs.so plus declared generic PAL/config patches. The reference metadata/digest adapter is not compiled or installed. No general-token, FIPS, certification or persistent-token qualification.

Generic PAL replaces POSIX current-directory files and eight fixed labels with 256 process-local heap entries, exact byte labels 1..32 and same-label overwrite/handle reuse. Upstream object list capacity 128 and sessions 32. Label-only search, token-only objects and upstream template parsing remain unchanged. These are disclosed PKCS#11 semantic changes, not provisioning-only extensions.

All sessions of one loaded library share objects. PAL storage survives C_Finalize/C_Initialize in that library instance, but fresh independent exec/process starts empty; unloading/process exit ends access. Fork can inherit a memory snapshot and must not be used as independent token state. No shared-memory/persistence/restart-reopen claim. Use independent processes/instances per shard and client.

PAL privacy uses a DER first-child INTEGER heuristic instead of fixed private-key labels; CKA_CLASS/CKA_VALUE visibility changes. Snapshot reads, mutex-protected store, malloc/free with no secure erasure, destroy-and-reuse versus stock zeroing fallback; allocation/full-store errors and provider return values are preserved. See FILE-NOTICES.txt for all port/config deltas.

Real upstream Mbed TLS CTR-DRBG uses Linux platform entropy (getrandom or /dev/urandom). Static Mbed TLS 3.6.5 code is incorporated into the .so; ldd alone is not the complete content/license closure. Both FetchContent archives include URL/hash locks; configure/build are offline.

Native slot ID 1 is token-present index 0. C_GetInfo, C_GetSlotInfo, C_GetMechanismList, C_GetSessionInfo, C_Logout and C_Digest among others are NULL; C_GetTokenInfo returns OK without writing metadata. Missing queries remain missing, HMAC/CMAC advertisement and RSA flags are not normalized. Consumers must tolerate these upstream limits.

C_Login and C_InitToken are upstream no-op CKR_OK stubs: wrong PIN is accepted, token labels/PINs are not provisioned, and there is no native authentication boundary. Optional PIN/SO_PIN files are syntax-validated only, never logged or copied into token state; no PIN rejection claim.

P11LAB_LABEL defaults to P11Lab and is a 1..32 ASCII application/object hint (letters, digits, spaces, dot, underscore, hyphen), not native token metadata. init validates controls and module readability only; creates no files or token. health initializes a fresh standalone module, opens/closes a session, uses RNG and finalizes; it cannot attest to the app token. exec validates controls then preserves argv/exit status with no module preflight.

Provider token state needs no writable files or volume; arbitrary UID/read-only rootfs works with readable module and optional input files. Caller output mounts can be writable. No server/server-ready op. Application closes/finalizes and owns termination; new independent process supplies a fresh volatile store.

Checker module lives in each in-process test/file child with an independent store. Preferred proxy module lives in the daemon process (pinned proxy a348a5f59b535b1ca309ea9f0a722e3bec692f72: one logical client/trusted domain and one managed provider chain; max_contexts=1 is admission, not isolation); health/init are not its token. Raw metadata gaps can prevent installed checker/proxy lanes; record incomplete evidence/native failure without inventing metadata or verdicts.

Basic runtime excludes checker, Python, datasets, tracing, OpenSC and build tools. Optional consumer/checker/proxy derivatives have independent identities, actual-size evidence and admission. Migrated files have missing grants; root Apache-2.0 does not cover them; OASIS headers and all base/layer/source obligations still need review. Local-only/unreviewed.

distribution.reason: Local-only port: migrated PAL/config/allocator grants are missing; OASIS IPR, actual-content and digest-bound source-delivery review remain incomplete. No publication eligibility.
